```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = requireNamespace("Seurat", quietly = TRUE))
```

HIXscore computes three sample-level layer scores from single-cell RNA-seq and fuses them into **sysHIX**:
**E** (epithelial meta-programs), **C** (cell-level baseline-deviation modules) and **M** (immune/stromal cell-state
composition). This vignette runs on small *synthetic* data so that it takes seconds; the steps that need the
reference download, the annotation or the long BDM selection are shown but not run (`eval = FALSE`).

Supported: Seurat 4.3 - 4.4.

```{r library}
library(HIXscore)
```

## Step 0: reference data (not run)

The annotation transfers labels from a single-cell reference. By default the HIXscore reference (about 550 MB) is
downloaded once into the user cache and its md5 sum is checked.

```{r reference, eval = FALSE}
ref <- load_reference()                                    # download (cached), check, prepare
save_reference(ref, "HIXscore_reference_prepared.rds")     # optional: skip the preparation next time
ref <- load_reference(path = "HIXscore_reference_prepared.rds")
```

A reference of your own is a Seurat (v4) object with the raw counts in the `RNA` assay, a major-cell-type and a
cell-state metadata column (epithelial cells labelled `"Epithelial"`), and a PCA reduction with the embeddings of all cells
and the feature loadings. For modes 1 and 2 its cell states must include the 72 states of the shipped M-layer model.

```{r own-reference, eval = FALSE}
ref <- load_reference(path = "my_reference.rds", major_col = "celltype_major", minor_col = "cell_type2",
                      reduction = "pca", ref_features = NULL)
check_reference(ref)                                       # lists the M-layer states the reference lacks
```

## Step 1: annotate the cells (not run)

```{r annotate, eval = FALSE}
# obj: Seurat object with raw counts, all samples, unique cell names and a sample column
obj <- annotate_cells(obj, ref, sample_col = "sample_id", checkpoint_dir = "annotation_checkpoints")
attr(obj, "annotation_summary")
attr(obj, "annotation_failed")                             # samples that failed, with the reason
inp <- prepare_input(obj)                                  # log-normalise; split into epithelial / non-epithelial
epi <- inp$epi; tme <- inp$tme
```

Each sample is annotated on its own; a failing sample does not stop the others, and `checkpoint_dir` lets a repeated
call annotate only the missing samples. Use `minor_for = "all"` if you also need the epithelial states (BDM steps).

## Synthetic input

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
mp <- default_MP_list(); bdm <- default_BDM_programs(); states <- rownames(default_M_model()$W)
genes <- unique(c(unlist(mp), unlist(bdm), paste0("G", 1:2500)))
ns <- 12; per <- 45; n <- ns * per
sid <- paste0("s", rep(seq_len(ns), each = per))
tissue <- rep(c("NT", "PD", "PrCA"), each = ns / 3)[as.integer(sub("s", "", sid))]
mu <- rexp(length(genes), 0.5)
m <- matrix(rpois(length(genes) * n, rep(mu, n)), length(genes), n,
            dimnames = list(genes, paste0("c", seq_len(n))))
epi <- Seurat::NormalizeData(Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(m), verbose = FALSE)
epi$sample_id <- sid; epi$tissue <- tissue; epi$series <- paste0("ser", 1 + as.integer(sub("s", "", sid)) %% 4)
tme <- data.frame(sample_id = rep(paste0("s", seq_len(ns)), each = 250),
                  cell_state = sample(states, ns * 250, replace = TRUE))
```

## Step 2: `hixscore()` - modes 1 and 2

```{r mode1}
res <- hixscore(epi, tme, layers = "ALL", mode = "pretrained")
res$status
head(res$samples[, c("sample_id", "has_E", "has_C", "has_M", "has_sysHIX", "E_seHIX_z", "S_C_z", "S_M_z", "sysHIX")], 4)
```

`layers` selects what is computed (`"E"`, `"C"`, `"M"`, `"sysHIX"` or `"ALL"`). Each layer is scored on the samples that
pass its own filters (`min_cells_epi = 30`, `min_cells_tme = 200`); samples are intersected only for `sysHIX`.

Run the layers one at a time and pass the result as `previous` to reuse what is finished:

```{r layers}
r <- hixscore(epi, layers = "E")
r <- hixscore(epi, layers = "C", previous = r)
r <- hixscore(epi, tme, layers = "M", previous = r)
r <- hixscore(layers = "sysHIX", previous = r)
r$status
```

A layer that fails does not stop the others. Here the M layer cannot be scored because no cell state is in the model; E and
C are kept, `sysHIX` is skipped, and the layer can be repaired and the fusion added without recomputing E and C:

```{r failure, warning = FALSE}
bad <- tme; bad$cell_state <- "not_a_state"
r <- hixscore(epi, bad, layers = "ALL")
r$status[, c("layer", "status", "note")]
r <- hixscore(epi, tme, layers = c("M", "sysHIX"), previous = r)
r$status[, c("layer", "status")]
```

Mode 2 refits the E and C baselines and the scHIX thresholds on the NT samples of `epi`:

```{r mode2, warning = FALSE}
res2 <- hixscore(epi, tme, mode = "custom_baseline", tissue_col = "tissue", nt_label = "NT")
res2$info$n_nt_E_baseline
```

Fewer than 3 NT samples is an error and 3 - 9 gives a warning.

Your own E-layer gene sets are given with `mp_list` (named list; checked by `validate_MP_list()`). In mode 2 the E baseline is
fitted on these sets; in mode 1 the names must equal those of `default_MP_list()`.

```{r custom-mp, warning = FALSE}
my_mp <- default_MP_list()[1:4]; names(my_mp) <- paste0("MyMP_", seq_along(my_mp))
r_mp <- hixscore(epi, layers = "E", mode = "custom_baseline", mp_list = my_mp)
r_mp$status[, c("layer", "status")]
```

## Mode 3: `hixscore_train()`

The training steps can be run one by one or together; finished steps are reused through `previous`.

```{r mode3, warning = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE)}
labels <- data.frame(sample_id = paste0("s", seq_len(ns)), label = rep(c("NT", "Inflammatory", "Malignant"), each = ns / 3))
tr <- hixscore_train(epi, steps = c("E", "C"))                         # baselines
tr <- hixscore_train(epi, tme, labels, steps = "fusion", previous = tr,
                     levels = c("NT", "Inflammatory", "Malignant"))     # fusion model
tr$status
res3 <- hixscore(epi, tme, mode = "custom_baseline", model = tr$model, E_baseline = tr$E_baseline,
                 C_baseline = tr$C_baseline, M_model = tr$M_model)
range(res3$samples$sysHIX, na.rm = TRUE)
```

With two classes (`levels = c("NT", "Disease")`) the fusion is a logistic regression and sysHIX is the probability of
disease (0 - 1). The returned training sysHIX is computed on the samples the fusion model was fitted on.

### M layer from your data

```{r mlayer, eval = FALSE}
tr <- hixscore_train(tme = tme, steps = "M_scan", M_model = "derive")  # NMF rank scan
tr$scans$M                                                             # cophenetic correlation per rank
tr <- hixscore_train(tme = tme, steps = "M", M_model = "derive", M_k = "auto", previous = tr)
```

Your own weight matrix `W` (states x CMs, non-negative, row names = states) is given with `M_W`; no rank scan is run:

```{r mw, eval = FALSE}
tr <- hixscore_train(tme = tme, steps = "M", M_W = W)
```

`M_k = "auto"` takes the rank with rho(k-2) < rho(k-1) < rho(k) and rho(k) > rho(k+1) for the cophenetic correlation rho.

### BDM gene sets from your data (not run)

The selection needs the raw counts, the sample, tissue and `series` columns and the epithelial state of each cell
(annotate with `minor_for = "all"`; the state column is `predicted.minor`). The number of modules is chosen from the
stability table, so the work is split into two steps.

```{r bdm, eval = FALSE}
tr <- hixscore_train(epi, steps = "BDM_scan", programs = "derive", bdm_state_col = "predicted.minor",
                     bdm_args = list(), bdm_maxK = 10, bdm_reps = 200)     # the slow part
tr$scans$bdm$stability                                                      # choose bdm_k
tr <- hixscore_train(epi, steps = "BDM", programs = "derive", bdm_k = 5, previous = tr)
tr$programs                                                                 # Module_1 ... gene symbols

# then the remaining steps with these programs
tr <- hixscore_train(epi, tme, labels, steps = c("E", "C", "fusion"), programs = tr$programs, previous = tr)
```

`bdm_args` takes the arguments of the selection steps: `max_var`, `min_freq`, `min_fc`, `min_consistency`,
`min_disease_types`, `min_cells`, `min_logcpm` and others (see `?bdm_constrained_genes`, `?bdm_deviation_genes`,
`?bdm_pseudobulk`). The selection is repeated leaving each cohort (`series`) out and needs at least 2 cohorts with more
than 5 samples.

### Your own BDM gene sets (mode 3)

Instead of selecting the gene sets from your data, pass them as a named list: `programs = list(Module_1 = c(...), Module_2 = c(...))`
with at least 2 sets, at least 5 genes each and unique names. `validate_BDM_programs()` checks the list (and, with `genes =`,
warns when less than 70% of a set is present in your data). The model is trained with these sets, and the same sets
have to be used for scoring: `hixscore()` takes them together with the components of that training run.

```{r own-bdm, warning = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE)}
my_bdm <- setNames(unname(bdm[1:3]), paste0("MyModule_", 1:3))
my_bdm <- validate_BDM_programs(my_bdm, genes = rownames(epi))
tr_b <- hixscore_train(epi, tme, labels, steps = c("E", "C", "fusion"), programs = my_bdm,
                       levels = c("NT", "Inflammatory", "Malignant"))
res_b <- hixscore(epi, tme, mode = "custom_baseline", model = tr_b$model, E_baseline = tr_b$E_baseline,
                  C_baseline = tr_b$C_baseline, M_model = tr_b$M_model, programs = tr_b$programs)
names(tr_b$programs)
res_b$status[, c("layer", "status")]
```

## Evaluate

```{r eval, eval = requireNamespace("pROC", quietly = TRUE)}
ev <- evaluate_scores(res$samples, stages = c(NT = "NT", PD = "non-malignant", PrCA = "malignant"), min_n = 1)
ev$auc_nt_vs_disease
```
